reasons: No tests are visible in this file.
A comment in another file refers to a client copy of this list, so the two copies could drift apart. This was not checked here.

terms.meaning: A step in a project's life, such as planning, under construction, operating, or cancelled.
A named visual style for a label, such as neutral, active, warn, dead or retired.
A small coloured label that shows a value at a glance.

used_by: the ingest conformer (named in a comment)

sections.name: LifecycleTone
sections.title: Allowed visual tones
sections.what: Defines the five visual tones a lifecycle stage can have: neutral, active, warn, dead and retired. These decide how a stage appears on screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps badge colours to a fixed set so the look stays consistent.
sections.watch_out: Adding a tone here also needs a matching entry in the style table, or badges with that tone will have no style.

sections.name: LIFECYCLE_META
sections.title: Lifecycle stages with labels and tones
sections.what: Lists every known project stage with its display name and tone, and the comments explain how some stages relate. OPERATING and OPERATIONAL are treated as the same idea, and RETIRED is kept separate from CANCELLED.
sections.why: The comments explain the choices: retired units are a finished state, not a cancelled project, and the financial investment decision is a milestone, not a stage.
sections.watch_out: Any code added here is accepted by the ingest step at once, so a typo added here becomes a valid stage.

sections.name: formatLifecycleStage
sections.title: Turn stage code into readable label
sections.what: Converts a stage code into the label shown on screen. Known stages use their set label, unknown codes are rewritten with spaces and capital letters, and an empty stage shows a not-applicable marker.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a new stage show something readable before anyone adds it to the list.
sections.watch_out: Unknown codes are shown without any check, so a bad code looks like a real stage on screen.

sections.name: lifecycleTone
sections.title: Look up tone for a stage
sections.what: Returns the tone for a stage, or neutral when the stage is empty or unknown.
sections.why: Likely reason: a neutral fallback keeps unknown stages from breaking the page.
sections.watch_out: An unknown or misspelled stage looks neutral, which can hide a data error.

sections.name: TONE_CLASSES
sections.title: Style classes for each tone
sections.what: Maps each tone to the styling classes that colour a badge. The warn tone uses the amber status colour, the dead tone uses red with a strike-through, and the others use neutral or primary colours.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps visual styling separate from the meaning of each stage.
sections.watch_out: Class names must exist in the styling setup, or the badge shows no colour and no error.

sections.name: lifecycleBadgeClass
sections.title: Badge style for a stage
sections.what: Combines the tone lookup and the style table to give the badge classes for a stage. Pages call this to draw a stage badge.
sections.why: Likely reason: one call saves each page from repeating the tone lookup.
sections.watch_out: An empty stage gets the neutral badge through the fallback, so a missing stage can look normal.

summary: Holds the list of project lifecycle stages with their display names and colour tones, plus helpers that turn a stage code into a readable label and a badge style.
purpose: Gives every screen one shared way to show a project's stage, so the same stage looks the same everywhere.
why: Likely reason: keeps stage labels and colours in one place so pages agree with each other.
how: First, a fixed table maps each stage code to a label and a tone. Then the list of valid codes is built from that table. Helpers look up the label, the tone, and the badge style, and fall back to a plain display for unknown stages.
inputs: A stage code as text, which may be empty or unknown.
outputs: A readable label, a tone name, or a set of style classes for a badge.
risks: Changing a code or tone here changes how existing stored stages look. The stage list is also used to accept stages during ingest, so adding a code makes it accepted there at once.
debug: If a stage shows a raw code instead of a label, that code is missing from the table. If a badge has no colour, check that its tone name exists in the style table.
